title: DumpDetective Observation
description: The fusion wire format: DumpDetective.Sdk.Observations.Observation as it actually serializes today via System.Text.Json with { PropertyNamingPolicy = CamelCase, Converters = { JsonStringEnumConverter } } — the exact options TraceReportWriter uses to write report.json (src/DumpDetective.Cli/Output/TraceReportWriter.cs). Verified empirically against a live build of DumpDetective.Sdk on 2026-09-09, not hand-derived from the C# source alone — see the 'Wire-format gotchas' notes below for the non-obvious results of that check. This is the real, shipped shape of trace-session report.json's `observations` array today; it is not a forward-looking design document.
notes: GOTCHA 1 — mixed casing: PropertyNamingPolicy.CamelCase only renames property *names* (id, observationType, ...). Every enum (Kind, Fidelity, MeasureUnit, MeasureSemantics, AnchorConfidence, TemporalKind, FidelityLevel) carries its own [JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))] with no naming policy, so enum *values* serialize in their literal C# casing ("Method", "Exact", "Interval", "Full"), not camelCase. Property names are camelCase; enum values are PascalCase. Both are correct — do not 'fix' one to match the other.

GOTCHA 2 — $kind vs kind: EntityRef's [JsonPolymorphic] discriminator ($kind, e.g. "method") is only emitted when a value is serialized through a property declared as the abstract EntityRef type — which is only true for Observation.Subjects. A field declared as a concrete subtype (MethodRef.DeclaringType : TypeRef, TypeRef.Module : ModuleRef?) never gets a $kind, even though it carries the same 'kind' property. A consumer parsing entities nested inside subjects (declaringType, module) must not expect $kind there.

GOTCHA 3 — wrapper types, not bare strings: ArtifactId, Capability, and ObservationId are all single-field record structs with no custom converter, so each serializes as a one-key object ({"value":"..."} for ArtifactId/ObservationId, {"key":"..."} for Capability), never as a bare JSON string.

GOTCHA 4 — ObservationId.ToString() lies: the type overrides ToString() to return Guid 'N' format (no hyphens), used nowhere in JSON serialization. The wire value is the Guid's default System.Text.Json representation (hyphenated 'D' format, e.g. "5dedca19-ade3-45b7-bed6-726f92d31d80").

GOTCHA 5 — 64-bit handles as JSON numbers: ulong fields (ObjectRef.Address, TypeRef.MethodTable, MethodRef.MethodDesc, ModuleRef.ModuleAddress) serialize as plain JSON numeric literals with full precision. A JS/TS consumer using JSON.parse will silently lose precision above 2^53 — heap addresses on a 64-bit process routinely exceed that. Any UI/Phase 8 consumer must parse these as strings or a BigInt-safe parser, not JSON.parse's default number handling.
TimeSpan fields (TimeAnchor.ProcessUptime) serialize via .NET's constant ('c') TimeSpan format, e.g. "00:00:01" or "1.02:03:04.5000000" for a value spanning more than a day.

capability.description: Capability — see GOTCHA 3. Key must be a member of capability-registry.json.

typeRefBody.description: TypeRef fields when nested via a concretely-typed property (no $kind — see GOTCHA 2).

entityRef.description: Only shape used for Observation.Subjects elements — carries $kind (see GOTCHA 2).

measure.description: Must be a raw fact, never a weighted composite — see Observation.cs's purity-rules remark.

observationType.description: Free-form per Observation.cs by design; the checked-in list of types actually emitted today lives in observation-type-registry.json, not as a closed enum here.
